sanskrit: taṃ tu rāmaḥ samāśvāsya bhrātaraṃ guruvatsalam lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā praṣṭuṃ samupacakrame
english: Then Rāma, having comforted that brother who revered his elders, began, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, to question him.

sanskrit: kim etad iccheyam ahaṃ śrotuṃ pravyāhṛtaṃ tvayā yasmāt tvam āgato deśam imaṃ cīrajaṭājinī
english: "What is this that I wish to hear from your own lips—why have you come to this region dressed in bark-cloth, matted locks, and a black-antelope hide?"

sanskrit: yannimittam imaṃ deśaṃ kṛṣṇājinajaṭādharaḥ hitvā rājyaṃ praviṣṭas tvaṃ tat sarvaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: "For what reason have you, wearing a black-antelope skin and matted hair, abandoned the kingdom and entered this forest? You should tell me everything."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ kekayīputraḥ kākutsthena mahātmanā pragṛhya balavad bhūyaḥ prāñjalir vākyam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Kākutstha, the son of Kaikeyī, clasping his hands firmly in reverence once more, spoke these words:

sanskrit: āryaṃ tātaḥ parityajya kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram gataḥ svargaṃ mahābāhuḥ putraśokābhipīḍitaḥ
english: "The noble father, the long-armed one, abandoning virtue and performing a most terrible deed, has gone to heaven, tormented by grief for his son."

sanskrit: striyā niyuktaḥ kaikeyyā mama mātrā paraṃtapa cakāra sumahat pāpam idam ātmayaśoharam
english: "Commanded by a woman—Kaikeyī, my own mother, O scorcher of foes—he committed this great sin that destroys one's own renown."

sanskrit: sā rājyaphalam aprāpya vidhavā śokakarśitā patiṣyati mahāghore niraye jananī mama
english: "She, having failed to reap the fruit of the kingdom, widowed and emaciated by grief, my mother will fall into a most dreadful hell."

sanskrit: tasya me dāsabhūtasya prasādaṃ kartum arhasi abhiṣiñcasva cādyaiva rājyena maghavān iva
english: "You should show grace to me who am your slave. Consecrate yourself today with the kingdom, as Maghavān [Indra] was consecrated."

sanskrit: imāḥ prakṛtayaḥ sarvā vidhavā māturaś ca yāḥ tvat sakāśam anuprāptāḥ prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "All these subjects, and those mothers who are now widowed, have come to your presence; you should show them your grace."

sanskrit: tadānupūrvyā yuktaṃ ca yuktaṃ cātmani mānada rājyaṃ prāpnuhi dharmeṇa sakāmān suhṛdaḥ kuru
english: "It is both fitting by succession and fitting in yourself, O giver of honour—take the kingdom by dharma and fulfil the wishes of your friends."

sanskrit: bhavatv avidhavā bhūmiḥ samagrā patinā tvayā śaśinā vimaleneva śāradī rajanī yathā
english: "Let the whole earth be without widowhood, with you as its lord, as an autumnal night is [made full] by the unstained moon."

sanskrit: ebhiś ca sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ śirasā yācito mayā bhrātuḥ śiṣyasya dāsasya prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "Implored with bowed head by me, together with these ministers, you should show grace to a brother, a pupil, a slave."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ śāśvataṃ pitryaṃ sarvaṃ sacivamaṇḍalam pūjitaṃ puruṣavyāghra nātikramitum utsahe
english: "This entire council of ministers, our father's perpetual [retinue], is honoured, O tiger among men; I dare not transgress them."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhuḥ sabāṣpaḥ kekayīsutaḥ rāmasya śirasā pādau jagrāha bharataḥ punaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Bharata, the long-armed son of Kaikeyī, with tears in his eyes, grasped Rāma's feet with his head [bowed] once more.

sanskrit: taṃ mattam iva mātaṅgaṃ niḥśvasantaṃ punaḥ punaḥ bhrātaraṃ bharataṃ rāmaḥ pariṣvajyedam abravīt
english: Embracing that brother Bharata, who was sighing again and again like a rutting elephant, Rāma spoke thus:

sanskrit: kulīnaḥ sattvasaṃpannas tejasvī caritavrataḥ rājyahetoḥ kathaṃ pāpam ācaret tvadvidho janaḥ
english: "How could a person like you—well-born, endowed with virtue, splendid, faithful to your vows—commit a sin for the sake of a kingdom?"

sanskrit: na doṣaṃ tvayi paśyāmi sūkṣmam apy ari sūdana na cāpi jananīṃ bālyāt tvaṃ vigarhitum arhasi
english: "I see not even the slightest fault in you, O slayer of enemies; nor indeed should you reproach your mother out of childish impulse."

sanskrit: yāvat pitari dharmajña gauravaṃ lokasatkṛte tāvad dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha jananyām api gauravam
english: "O knower of dharma, O best of those who bear dharma, the reverence owed to a mother honoured by the world is equal to that owed to a father."

sanskrit: etābhyāṃ dharmaśīlābhyāṃ vanaṃ gaccheti rāghava mātā pitṛbhyām ukto 'haṃ katham anyat samācare
english: "Being told by both of these two who are devoted to dharma—mother and father—'Go to the forest, O Rāghava,' how could I do otherwise?"

sanskrit: tvayā rājyam ayodhyāyāṃ prāptavyaṃ lokasatkṛtam vastavyaṃ daṇḍakāraṇye mayā valkalavāsasā
english: "The kingdom of Ayodhyā, honoured by the world, is to be received by you; the Daṇḍaka forest is to be dwelt in by me, clothed in bark."

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtvā mahārājo vibhāgaṃ lokasaṃnidhau vyādiśya ca mahātejā divaṃ daśaratho gataḥ
english: "Having thus made this division and given these commands before the assembly of the world, the great-spirited, mighty king Daśaratha went to heaven."

sanskrit: sa ca pramāṇaṃ dharmātmā rājā lokagurus tava pitrā dattaṃ yathābhāgam upabhoktuṃ tvam arhasi
english: "He, the dharma-souled king, teacher of the world, is the authority for you; you ought to enjoy the portion given by your father as is proper."

sanskrit: caturdaśa samāḥ saumya daṇḍakāraṇyam āśritaḥ upabhokṣye tv ahaṃ dattaṃ bhāgaṃ pitrā mahātmanā
english: "For fourteen years, gentle one, dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest, I shall enjoy the portion given to me by the great-souled father."

sanskrit: yad abravīn māṃ naralokasatkṛtaḥ pitā mahātmā vibudhādhipopamaḥ tad eva manye paramātmano hitaṃ na sarvalokeśvarabhāvam avyayam
english: "What the great-souled father, honoured among men, comparable to the lord of the gods, said to me—that alone I consider to be the highest good of the soul, not the imperishable lordship over all the worlds."

sanskrit: tataḥ puruṣasiṃhānāṃ vṛtānāṃ taiḥ suhṛdgaṇaiḥ śocatām eva rajanī duḥkhena vyatyavartata
english: Then, for those lions among men surrounded by their bands of friends, grieving all the while, the night passed in sorrow.

sanskrit: rajanyāṃ suprabhātāyāṃ bhrātaras te suhṛdvṛtāḥ mandākinyāṃ hutaṃ japyaṃ kṛtvā rāmam upāgaman
english: When the night had brightened into a fair dawn, those brothers, accompanied by their friends, having offered oblations and performed japa at the Mandākinī, approached Rāma.

sanskrit: tūṣṇīṃ te samupāsīnā na kaś cit kiṃ cid abravīt bharatas tu suhṛnmadhye rāmavacanam abravīt
english: They sat in silence; no one said anything. But Bharata, in the midst of his friends, spoke a reply to Rāma's words:

sanskrit: sāntvitā māmikā mātā dattaṃ rājyam idaṃ mama tad dadāmi tavaivāhaṃ bhuṅkṣva rājyam akaṇṭakam
english: "My mother has been appeased; this kingdom was given to me. I give it back to you yourself—enjoy the kingdom free of thorns."

sanskrit: mahatevāmbuvegena bhinnaḥ setur jalāgame durāvāraṃ tvadanyena rājyakhaṇḍam idaṃ mahat
english: "Like a dam broken by the great force of water at the onset of rains, this great realm is impossible for anyone but you to hold."

sanskrit: gatiṃ khara ivāśvasya tārkṣyasyeva patatriṇaḥ anugantuṃ na śaktir me gatiṃ tava mahīpate
english: "I have no power to follow your pace, O lord of the earth—as a donkey cannot match the pace of a horse, nor a common bird match Tārkṣya [Garuḍa]."

sanskrit: sujīvaṃ nityaśas tasya yaḥ parair upajīvyate rāma tena tu durjīvaṃ yaḥ parān upajīvati
english: "O Rāma, easy indeed is the life of one who is always depended upon by others; but hard is the life of one who depends upon others."

sanskrit: yathā tu ropito vṛkṣaḥ puruṣeṇa vivardhitaḥ hrasvakena durāroho rūḍhaskandho mahādrumaḥ
english: "Just as a tree planted and nurtured by a man, having grown with a sturdy trunk into a great tree, becomes too tall for that same small man to climb—

sanskrit: sa yadā puṣpito bhūtvā phalāni na vidarśayet sa tāṃ nānubhavet prītiṃ yasya hetoḥ prabhāvitaḥ
english: "—and when that tree, having bloomed, yields him no fruit, he does not enjoy the delight for whose sake he caused it to flourish—

sanskrit: eṣopamā mahābāho tvam arthaṃ vettum arhasi yadi tvam asmān ṛṣabho bhartā bhṛtyān na śādhi hi
english: "—such is this simile, O long-armed one; you ought to understand its meaning: if you, the bull among men, the lord, do not govern us your servants, then indeed—"

sanskrit: śreṇayas tvāṃ mahārāja paśyantv agryāś ca sarvaśaḥ pratapantam ivādityaṃ rājye sthitam ariṃdamam
english: "O great king, let the guilds and chief men everywhere behold you, standing in the kingdom blazing like the sun, O subduer of enemies."

sanskrit: tavānuyāne kākutṣṭha mattā nardantu kuñjarāḥ antaḥpura gatā nāryo nandantu susamāhitāḥ
english: "In your retinue, O Kākutstha, let intoxicated elephants trumpet; let the women of the inner apartments rejoice with great composure."

sanskrit: tasya sādhv ity amanyanta nāgarā vividhā janāḥ bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvā rāmaṃ pratyanuyācataḥ
english: Having heard Bharata's words, the townspeople and various other folk thought them good and joined in imploring Rāma.

sanskrit: tam evaṃ duḥkhitaṃ prekṣya vilapantaṃ yaśasvinam rāmaḥ kṛtātmā bharataṃ samāśvāsayad ātmavān
english: Seeing that illustrious one thus afflicted and lamenting, Rāma, self-mastered and resolved in spirit, comforted Bharata.

sanskrit: nātmanaḥ kāmakāro 'sti puruṣo 'yam anīśvaraḥ itaś cetarataś cainaṃ kṛtāntaḥ parikarṣati
english: "This person is not lord of himself; he has no power to act at will. Fate drags him this way and that."

sanskrit: sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ ca jīvitam
english: "All accumulations end in dissolution; all that rises ends in a fall; all unions end in separation; life ends in death."

sanskrit: yathā phalānaṃ pakvānāṃ nānyatra patanād bhayam evaṃ narasya jātasya nānyatra maraṇād bhayam
english: "As for ripe fruits there is no fear other than falling, so for a man who is born there is no fear other than death."

sanskrit: yathāgāraṃ dṛḍhasthūṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ bhūtvāvasīdati tathāvasīdanti narā jarāmṛtyuvaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: "Just as a house with firm pillars, having grown old, crumbles down, so men crumble, having fallen under the power of old age and death."

sanskrit: ahorātrāṇi gacchanti sarveṣāṃ prāṇinām iha āyūṃṣi kṣapayanty āśu grīṣme jalam ivāṃśavaḥ
english: "The days and nights pass for all living beings here, swiftly consuming their life-spans, as the sun's rays consume water in summer."

sanskrit: ātmānam anuśoca tvaṃ kim anyam anuśocasi āyus te hīyate yasya sthitasya ca gatasya ca
english: "Grieve for yourself—why do you grieve for another? Your life-span diminishes whether you stand still or move on."

sanskrit: sahaiva mṛtyur vrajati saha mṛtyur niṣīdati gatvā sudīrgham adhvānaṃ saha mṛtyur nivartate
english: "Death walks together with one; death sits down together; having gone a very long road, death turns back together with one."

sanskrit: gātreṣu valayaḥ prāptāḥ śvetāś caiva śiroruhāḥ jarayā puruṣo jīrṇaḥ kiṃ hi kṛtvā prabhāvayet
english: "Wrinkles have come upon the limbs, and the hair has turned white; the man, worn out by old age—what great deed can he now accomplish?"

sanskrit: nandanty udita āditye nandanty astam ite ravau ātmano nāvabudhyante manuṣyā jīvitakṣayam
english: "Men rejoice at the sun's rising and rejoice at the sun's setting, yet they do not perceive the waning of their own life."

sanskrit: hṛṣyanty ṛtumukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā navaṃ navam ihāgatam ṛtūnāṃ parivartena prāṇināṃ prāṇasaṃkṣayaḥ
english: "They delight upon seeing the new, ever-fresh turn of seasons arrive here; yet with the revolution of the seasons, the life-breath of living beings is eroded."

sanskrit: yathā kāṣṭhaṃ ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca sameyātāṃ mahārṇave sametya ca vyapeyātāṃ kālam āsādya kaṃ cana
english: "As two pieces of driftwood come together on the great ocean, and then, at the appointed time, drift apart again—

sanskrit: evaṃ bhāryāś ca putrāś ca jñātayaś ca vasūni ca sametya vyavadhāvanti dhruvo hy eṣāṃ vinābhavaḥ
english: "—so wives and sons and kinsmen and possessions come together and scatter apart; their separation is certain."

sanskrit: nātra kaś cid yathā bhāvaṃ prāṇī samabhivartate tena tasmin na sāmarthyaṃ pretasyāsty anuśocataḥ
english: "Here no living being abides as one might wish; therefore there is no power in lamenting for one who has departed."

sanskrit: yathā hi sārthaṃ gacchantaṃ brūyāt kaś cit pathi sthitaḥ aham apy āgamiṣyāmi pṛṣṭhato bhavatām iti
english: "Just as someone standing on the road might say to a caravan setting out, 'I too shall come after you'—

sanskrit: evaṃ pūrvair gato mārgaḥ pitṛpaitāmaho dhruvaḥ tam āpannaḥ kathaṃ śoced yasya nāsti vyatikramaḥ
english: "—so this road, trodden by those who went before us, the road of fathers and grandfathers, is certain. Having entered upon it—how should one grieve over what admits of no deviation?"

sanskrit: vayasaḥ patamānasya srotaso vānivartinaḥ ātmā sukhe niyoktavyaḥ sukhabhājaḥ prajāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: "When age is falling away like a stream that does not turn back, the self must be employed in what is good; creatures are said to be partakers of happiness."

sanskrit: dharmātmā sa śubhaiḥ kṛtsnaiḥ kratubhiś cāptadakṣiṇaiḥ dhūtapāpo gataḥ svargaṃ pitā naḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: "Our father, that dharma-souled lord of the earth, having performed all the auspicious sacrifices with full dakṣiṇā offerings and shaken off his sins, has gone to heaven."

sanskrit: bhṛtyānāṃ bharaṇāt samyak prajānāṃ paripālanāt arthādānāc ca dhārmeṇa pitā nas tridivaṃ gataḥ
english: "Through properly supporting his servants, through protecting his subjects, and through righteous acquisition of wealth, our father has gone to the three heavens."

sanskrit: iṣṭvā bahuvidhair yajñair bhogāṃś cāvāpya puṣkalān uttamaṃ cāyur āsādya svar gataḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: "Having worshipped with many kinds of sacrifice, having obtained abundant enjoyments, and having attained the utmost span of life, the lord of the earth has gone to heaven."

sanskrit: sa jīrṇaṃ mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ parityajya pitā hi naḥ daivīm ṛddhim anuprāpto brahmalokavihāriṇīm
english: "Our father, having abandoned the worn-out human body, has attained divine prosperity—that which courses through the world of Brahmā."

sanskrit: taṃ tu naivaṃ vidhaḥ kaś cit prājñaḥ śocitum arhati tvadvidho yadvidhaś cāpi śrutavān buddhimattaraḥ
english: "No wise person of such qualities as his ought to grieve for him—and still less someone like you, who is learned and endowed with greater intelligence."

sanskrit: ete bahuvidhāḥ śokā vilāpa rudite tathā varjanīyā hi dhīreṇa sarvāvasthāsu dhīmatā
english: "These manifold griefs, lamentations, and weeping are indeed to be avoided by the steadfast and wise man in all circumstances."

sanskrit: sa svastho bhava mā śoco yātvā cāvasa tāṃ purīm tathā pitrā niyukto 'si vaśinā vadatāmv vara
english: "Therefore be at peace, do not grieve; go and dwell in that city. You have been commanded thus by the self-controlled father, O best of those who speak."

sanskrit: yatrāham api tenaiva niyuktaḥ puṇyakarmaṇā tatraivāhaṃ kariṣyāmi pitur āryasya śāsanam
english: "And where I too have been commanded by that same one of meritorious deeds, there I shall carry out the command of the noble father."

sanskrit: na mayā śāsanaṃ tasya tyaktuṃ nyāyyam ariṃdama tat tvayāpi sadā mānyaṃ sa vai bandhuḥ sa naḥ pitā
english: "It is not right for me to abandon his command, O subduer of enemies; and it must always be honoured by you as well—he is truly our kinsman, he is our father."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu virate rāme vacanam arthavat uvāca bharataś citraṃ dhārmiko dhārmikaṃ vacaḥ
english: When Rāma had spoken thus and fell silent, his meaningful words concluded, the righteous Bharata spoke a remarkable, righteous speech:

sanskrit: ko hi syād īdṛśo loke yādṛśas tvam ariṃdama na tvāṃ pravyathayed duḥkhaṃ prītir vā na praharṣayet
english: "Who in this world could be like you, O subduer of enemies? Neither sorrow disturbs you, nor does joy elate you."

sanskrit: saṃmataś cāsi vṛddhānāṃ tāṃś ca pṛcchasi saṃśayān yathā mṛtas tathā jīvan yathāsati tathā sati
english: "You are honoured by the elders, and you seek out their counsel in matters of doubt. In death as in life, in adversity as in prosperity—you are the same."

sanskrit: yasyaiṣa buddhilābhaḥ syāt paritapyeta kena saḥ sa evaṃ vyasanaṃ prāpya na viṣīditum arhati
english: "One who has attained such wisdom—by what could he be tormented? Having encountered adversity thus, he ought not to be dejected."

sanskrit: amaropamasattvas tvaṃ mahātmā satyasaṃgaraḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī ca buddhimāṃś cāsi rāghava
english: "You are of a nature comparable to an immortal, O great-souled one, true to your vows, all-knowing, all-seeing, and wise, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: na tvām evaṃ guṇair yuktaṃ prabhavābhavakovidam aviṣahyatamaṃ duḥkham āsādayitum arhati
english: "Unbearable suffering ought not to befall you who are endowed with such qualities and who are skilled in understanding rise and fall."

sanskrit: proṣite mayi yat pāpaṃ mātrā matkāraṇāt kṛtam kṣudrayā tad aniṣṭaṃ me prasīdatu bhavān mama
english: "The sinful act committed by my petty mother on my account in my absence—that unwanted deed: may you show grace to me regarding it."

sanskrit: dharmabandhena baddho 'smi tenemāṃ neha mātaram hanmi tīvreṇa daṇḍena daṇḍārhāṃ pāpakāriṇīm
english: "I am bound by the bond of dharma, and therefore I do not slay this mother of mine here with severe punishment, though she who committed the sin deserves punishment."

sanskrit: kathaṃ daśarathāj jātaḥ śuddhābhijanakarmaṇaḥ jānan dharmam adharmiṣṭhaṃ kuryāṃ karma jugupsitam
english: "How could I, born of Daśaratha of pure lineage and deeds, knowing dharma, perform a most unrighteous and reprehensible act?"

sanskrit: guruḥ kriyāvān vṛddhaś ca rājā pretaḥ piteti ca tātaṃ na parigarheyaṃ daivataṃ ceti saṃsadi
english: "I would not censure our father in any assembly—he was an elder, a man of sacred rites, aged, a departed king, a father, a deity."

sanskrit: ko hi dharmārthayor hīnam īdṛśaṃ karma kilbiṣam striyāḥ priyacikīrṣuḥ san kuryād dharmajña dharmavit
english: "O knower of dharma, O one who understands dharma—who, desiring to please a woman, would perform such a sinful deed devoid of dharma and righteous purpose?"

sanskrit: antakāle hi bhūtāni muhyantīti purāśrutiḥ rājñaivaṃ kurvatā loke pratyakṣā sā śrutiḥ kṛtā
english: "The ancient saying is that creatures become bewildered at the time of death; through the king's acting thus, that saying has been made manifest in the world."

sanskrit: sādhv artham abhisaṃdhāya krodhān mohāc ca sāhasāt tātasya yad atikrāntaṃ pratyāharatu tad bhavān
english: "Having regard for a good purpose, may you reverse and undo what our father transgressed out of anger, delusion, and rashness."

sanskrit: pitur hi samatikrāntaṃ putro yaḥ sādhu manyate tad apatyaṃ mataṃ loke viparītam ato 'nyathā
english: "A son who regards his father's transgression as a proper thing—that is considered an offspring in the eyes of the world; otherwise the opposite is true."

sanskrit: tad apatyaṃ bhavān astu mā bhavān duṣkṛtaṃ pituḥ abhipat tat kṛtaṃ karma loke dhīravigarhitam
english: "May you be that offspring; do not ratify the misdeed of your father—that act, censured by the wise in this world."

sanskrit: kaikeyīṃ māṃ ca tātaṃ ca suhṛdo bāndhavāṃś ca naḥ paurajānapadān sarvāṃs trātu sarvam idaṃ bhavān
english: "May you deliver Kaikeyī, and me, and our father, and our friends and kinsmen, and all the townspeople and country-dwellers—may you deliver all this."

sanskrit: kva cāraṇyaṃ kva ca kṣātraṃ kva jaṭāḥ kva ca pālanam īdṛśaṃ vyāhataṃ karma na bhavān kartum arhasi
english: "What place does the forest have, and what place does kṣatriya duty have? What place do matted locks have, and what place does governance have? You ought not to perform this contradictory action."

sanskrit: atha kleśajam eva tvaṃ dharmaṃ caritum icchasi dharmeṇa caturo varṇān pālayan kleśam āpnuhi
english: "But if you wish to practise dharma arising from hardship, then endure hardship by protecting the four varṇas through dharma."

sanskrit: caturṇām āśramāṇāṃ hi gārhasthyaṃ śreṣṭham āśramam āhur dharmajña dharmajñās taṃ kathaṃ tyaktum arhasi
english: "Those who know dharma declare the householder's stage to be the best among the four stages of life, O knower of dharma—how can you abandon it?"

sanskrit: śrutena bālaḥ sthānena janmanā bhavato hy aham sa kathaṃ pālayiṣyāmi bhūmiṃ bhavati tiṣṭhati
english: "I am a child compared to you in learning, in position, and in birth. How shall I protect the earth while you stand by?"

sanskrit: hīnabuddhiguṇo bālo hīnaḥ sthānena cāpy aham bhavatā ca vinā bhūto na vartayitum utsahe
english: "I am a child of inferior intelligence and virtue, inferior in position; and being without you, I dare not maintain myself."

sanskrit: idaṃ nikhilam avyagraṃ pitryaṃ rājyam akaṇṭakam anuśādhi svadharmeṇa dharmajña saha bāndhavaiḥ
english: "Govern this entire, undivided, thorn-free paternal kingdom, O knower of dharma, by your own dharma, together with your kinsmen."

sanskrit: ihaiva tvābhiṣiñcantu dharmajña saha bāndhavaiḥ ṛtvijaḥ savasiṣṭhāś ca mantravan mantrakovidāḥ
english: "Let the officiating priests, including Vasiṣṭha, skilled in sacred formulas, consecrate you here, O knower of dharma, together with your kinsmen, with full ritual."

sanskrit: abhiṣiktas tvam asmābhir ayodhyāṃ pālane vraja vijitya tarasā lokān marudbhir iva vāsavaḥ
english: "Consecrated by us, go to Ayodhyā to govern it; having swiftly conquered the worlds, as Vāsava [Indra] with the Maruts."

sanskrit: ṛṇāni trīṇy apākurvan durhṛdaḥ sādhu nirdahan suhṛdas tarpayan kāmais tvam evātrānuśādhi mām
english: "Discharging the three debts, thoroughly burning away enemies, satisfying friends with desires—you alone govern, and govern me here."

sanskrit: adyārya muditāḥ santu suhṛdas te 'bhiṣecane adya bhītāḥ pālayantāṃ durhṛdas te diśo daśa
english: "Today, O noble one, let your friends rejoice at your consecration; today let your enemies, afraid, guard the ten directions."

sanskrit: ākrośaṃ mama mātuś ca pramṛjya puruṣarṣabha adya tatra bhavantaṃ ca pitaraṃ rakṣa kilbiṣāt
english: "Wiping away the reproach of my mother, O bull among men, protect yourself and our father today from sin."

sanskrit: śirasā tvābhiyāce 'haṃ kuruṣva karuṇāṃ mayi bāndhaveṣu ca sarveṣu bhūteṣv iva maheśvaraḥ
english: "With bowed head I beseech you: show compassion to me and to all kinsmen, as the great lord [Śiva] shows it to all beings."

sanskrit: atha vā pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā vanam eva bhavān itaḥ gamiṣyati gamiṣyāmi bhavatā sārdham apy aham
english: "Or else, if you shall go from here to the forest, turning your back on all this, I too shall go together with you."

sanskrit: tathāpi rāmo bharatena tāmyata prasādyamānaḥ śirasā mahīpatiḥ na caiva cakre gamanāya sattvavān matiṃ pitus tadvacane pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: Even so, Rāma, that lord of the earth, though earnestly implored by Bharata prostrating himself, did not form any intention of returning; steadfast in spirit, he stood firm in the command of his father.

sanskrit: tad adbhutaṃ sthairyam avekṣya rāghave samaṃ jano harṣam avāpa duḥkhitaḥ na yāty ayodhyām iti duḥkhito 'bhavat sthirapratijñatvam avekṣya harṣitaḥ
english: Beholding that extraordinary steadfastness in Rāghava, the people at once felt joy, yet being afflicted felt sorrow—sorrow that he would not go to Ayodhyā, yet joy upon seeing his firm resolution.

sanskrit: tam ṛtvijo naigamayūthavallabhās tathā visaṃjñāśrukalāś ca mātaraḥ tathā bruvāṇaṃ bharataṃ pratuṣṭuvuḥ praṇamya rāmaṃ ca yayācire saha
english: The officiating priests and the beloved leaders of the townspeople's companies, and the mothers, senseless with tears, praised Bharata as he spoke thus, and together bowed to Rāma and joined in imploring him.

sanskrit: punar evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu bharataṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ pratyuvaca tataḥ śrīmāñ jñātimadhye 'tisatkṛtaḥ
english: Then the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, the illustrious one greatly honoured in the midst of his kinsmen, replied to Bharata who was speaking thus once more:

sanskrit: upapannam idaṃ vākyaṃ yat tvam evam abhāṣathāḥ jātaḥ putro daśarathāt kaikeyyāṃ rājasattamāt
english: "This speech that you have delivered is fitting for one born a son of Daśaratha, the best of kings, upon Kaikeyī."

sanskrit: purā bhrātaḥ pitā naḥ sa mātaraṃ te samudvahan mātāmahe samāśrauṣīd rājyaśulkam anuttamam
english: "Long ago, brother, our father, when taking your mother as wife, promised your maternal grandfather an unequalled bride-price of a kingdom."

sanskrit: devāsure ca saṃgrāme jananyai tava pārthivaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭo dadau rājā varam ārādhitaḥ prabhuḥ
english: "And in the war of gods and demons, the lord king, greatly pleased and gratified, granted your mother a boon."

sanskrit: tataḥ sā saṃpratiśrāvya tava mātā yaśasvinī ayācata naraśreṣṭhaṃ dvau varau varavarṇinī
english: "Then your illustrious mother, having kept that boon in reserve, asked the best of men for two boons—she of excellent complexion."

sanskrit: tava rājyaṃ naravyāghra mama pravrājanaṃ tathā tac ca rājā tathā tasyai niyuktaḥ pradadau varam
english: "The kingdom for you, O tiger among men, and my banishment—and the king, bound by his word, granted her that boon accordingly."

sanskrit: tena pitrāham apy atra niyuktaḥ puruṣarṣabha caturdaśa vane vāsaṃ varṣāṇi varadānikam
english: "By that father, O bull among men, I too have been commanded here—as the gift of the boon—to dwell in the forest for fourteen years."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ vanam idaṃ prāpto nirjanaṃ lakṣmaṇānvitaḥ śītayā cāpratidvandvaḥ satyavāde sthitaḥ pituḥ
english: "So I have come to this solitary forest, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā, unrivalled in this, standing firm in the true word of my father."

sanskrit: bhavān api tathety eva pitaraṃ satyavādinam kartum arhati rājendraṃ kṣipram evābhiṣecanāt
english: "You likewise ought to make the king, that lord of kings who was true to his word, [come true in his word] swiftly through your consecration."

sanskrit: ṛṇān mocaya rājānaṃ matkṛte bharata prabhum pitaraṃ trāhi dharmajña mātaraṃ cābhinandaya
english: "Free the king, the lord, from debt on my behalf, O Bharata; save our father, O knower of dharma, and honour our mother."

sanskrit: śrūyate hi purā tāta śrutir gītā yaśasvinī gayena yajamānena gayeṣv eva pitṝn prati
english: "For it is heard, dear one, that long ago a glorious sacred text was sung by the sacrificer Gaya himself at Gayā, concerning the fathers:

sanskrit: puṃ nāmnā narakād yasmāt pitaraṃ trāyate sutaḥ tasmāt putra iti proktaḥ pitṝn yat pāti vā sutaḥ
english: "'Because a son delivers his father from the hell called Puṃ, therefore he is called putra [son]; or because a son protects the fathers.'"

sanskrit: eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā guṇavanto bahuśrutāḥ teṣāṃ vai samavetānām api kaś cid gayāṃ vrajet
english: "One should desire many sons, virtuous and learned; among them assembled together, may at least one go to Gayā."

sanskrit: evaṃ rājarṣayaḥ sarve pratītā rājanandana tasmāt trāhi naraśreṣṭha pitaraṃ narakāt prabho
english: "Thus all the royal seers were convinced, O delight of the king's line; therefore save our father from hell, O best of men, O lord."

sanskrit: ayodhyāṃ gaccha bharata prakṛtīr anurañjaya śatrughna sahito vīra saha sarvair dvijātibhiḥ
english: "Go to Ayodhyā, Bharata, please the subjects, O hero, together with Śatrughna and all the twice-born."

sanskrit: pravekṣye daṇḍakāraṇyam aham apy avilambayan ābhyāṃ tu sahito rājan vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca
english: "And I too shall enter the Daṇḍaka forest without delay, O king, accompanied by these two—Vaidehī and Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: tvaṃ rājā bhava bharata svayaṃ narāṇāṃ vanyānām aham api rājarāṇ mṛgāṇām gaccha tvaṃ puravaram adya saṃprahṛṣṭaḥ saṃhṛṣṭas tv aham api daṇḍakān pravekṣye
english: "You, Bharata, be king of men yourself; I too shall be king of the forest deer. Go to the best of cities today with joy; and I too, filled with joy, shall enter the Daṇḍakas."

sanskrit: chāyāṃ te dinakarabhāḥ prabādhamānaṃ varṣatraṃ bharata karotu mūrdhni śītām eteṣām aham api kānanadrumāṇāṃ chāyāṃ tām atiśayinīṃ sukhaṃ śrayiṣye
english: "Let the royal parasol, warding off the sun's rays, make cool shade upon your head, O Bharata; and I too shall happily take refuge in that surpassing cool shade of the forest trees."

sanskrit: śatrughnaḥ kuśalamatis tu te sahāyaḥ saumitrir mama viditaḥ pradhānamitram catvāras tanayavarā vayaṃ narendraṃ satyasthaṃ bharata carāma mā viṣādam
english: "Śatrughna of auspicious intelligence is your helper; Saumitri is known as my chief companion. We four, noble sons, O Bharata, serve the king who stood firm in truth—do not despair."
